For a service-to-product switch in India, the projects on your resume are where the interview starts.

Most portfolio advice says build more projects, or copy a big tutorial end to end. Both miss what happens next. The interviewer picks one line and asks you to defend a decision in it.

So build each project around the question it will draw. Each one below links to a free leetdata.ai problem that drills that exact question.

1️⃣ 𝗡𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗯𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵 𝗹𝗼𝗮𝗱
"The feed sent 3 updates for one product. Which row wins?"
https://leetdata.ai/problems/apply-daily-upserts

2️⃣ 𝗖𝗗𝗖 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲 𝗹𝗼𝗴
"Turn an append-only change log into one current row per user."
https://leetdata.ai/problems/keep-latest-record

3️⃣ 𝗖𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗸𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗺 𝗽𝗶𝗽𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲
"Where does one session end and the next begin?"
https://leetdata.ai/problems/session-detection

4️⃣ 𝗘𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝗷𝗼𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀

https://leetdata.ai/problems/deduplicate-before-join

5️⃣ 𝗗𝗮𝗶𝗹𝘆 𝗶𝗻𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝘀𝗻𝗮𝗽𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘁𝘀

https://leetdata.ai/problems/backfill-missing-snapshots

6️⃣ 𝗕𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗻 𝗵𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆 (𝗦𝗖𝗗 𝗧𝘆𝗽𝗲 𝟮)

https://leetdata.ai/problems/price-as-of-order

"Which rows should never reach the dashboard?"
https://leetdata.ai/problems/validate-data-quality

One finished project you can defend beats five you can only describe. Every problem runs in SQL, Python or PySpark, with hints and an editorial. No account needed.

Which of the 8 questions would stop you today?

Save this. Follow Data Engineering Weekly for more interview-ready lists.

inner, LEFT + IS NULL, anti-join, NOT IN + NULL trap, full outer, multi-condition, date range, many-to-many.

🧊 𝗟𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘀𝗲 𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗾𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻. 𝗡𝗼 𝘀𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗳𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁.

Two Spark jobs append to the same Iceberg table. Both start from snapshot 41. Job A commits first.

What happens to job B?

A) Its files overwrite job A's files

B) It retries its commit on top of the new snapshot, and both appends land

C) The table stays broken until someone runs compaction

D) Both commits succeed as two separate snapshots built on 41

Reply with one letter. We'll post the answer in the comments this evening.

📌 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗶𝘁 𝗴𝗲𝘁𝘀 𝗮𝘀𝗸𝗲𝗱
A pile of Parquet files on S3 isn't a table. In a table format the metadata decides what the table is, and every commit is one atomic metadata write. Commit races fall straight out of that.

Level 3 of the Lakehouse & Table Formats track on leetdata.ai is built around this exact race: two jobs, one table, a base snapshot that moved underneath you. Level 1 starts with a 7-minute primer and a screening quiz.

https://leetdata.ai/paths/lakehouse

#dataengineering #iceberg

Two jobs append to one Iceberg table from snapshot 41. A commits first. B:

A) overwrites A's files
B) retries on the new snapshot, both land
C) breaks it till compaction
D) forks into 2 snapshots

https://leetdata.ai/paths/lakehouse

🧹 𝟲 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮-𝗰𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 "𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗶𝘀 𝗮 𝗺𝗲𝘀𝘀" 𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱.

One Sunday morning's worth. DE interviews like a dirty table, because real pipelines start with one. Each of these is a free problem on leetdata.ai:

1️⃣ Column NULL Audit: profile a lead list before you trust it, NULL count and % per column

2️⃣ Fix Mixed-Case Join Keys: ' ACME CORP ', 'acme corp' and 'Acme corp ' are one account

3️⃣ Mixed Date Formats: '2024-03-05', '03/25/2024' and '2024/03/19' in the same column

4️⃣ Normalize Mixed Units: kg, lb and g, totalled per warehouse in kilograms

5️⃣ Clean Product Codes: split ELEC-10042-XL, and 00317 has to become 317

6️⃣ Dedupe, Keep the Most Complete Row: same email, keep the copy with the fewest NULLs

⚠️ 𝗡𝘂𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗿 𝟲 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗮𝗹𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗹𝗼𝘂𝗱.
"Keep any one" throws data away. Score each row by how many fields are filled, keep the highest, and break ties on the lowest contact_id. Say the tie-break before you write the query.

Hints and an editorial on every one. SQL runs in your browser, no signup.
